items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: I'm onstage with Sidney Bechet... Sidney Bechet, I had Sidney many times. In fact, I've got a story about Sidney. This was the first time I had Sidney. I hired him, I told him the date.

ctx.x: You had to stand in line.

Stand in line, just to sit in. And let me tell you something about drummers that you might be surprised to hear. We have a fellow by the name of Kansas around Chicago. And he supposedly was a tremendous drummer. Now, in those days, like I say, drums was not breaking it up and all that nonsense. And I'm onstage with Sidney Bechet. And somehow the drummer took the chorus, and when it got done it wasn't like when we started. We were a little -- the 32 bars were either 30 or 34, something had happened.

items.title: 67559_Art Hodes oral history interview
items.q: After the Blue Note gig and meeting Skank you decided to resettle in Chicago.

ctx.x: And had nothing. He just walked in cold with a cold lip.
After the Blue Note gig and meeting Skank you decided to resettle in Chicago.

I figured I could work half as hard and accomplish as much, as far as making a livelihood. There seemed to be enough work here. And I still have family here. And I decided to try it, and sent for my family and tried to settle here, see what was here.
